body:
> Found upgrading `french-tech-homies/pipao-v2` to 0.2.1 on 2026-09-01, using the `mcp visibility` check that
> shipped in that same release. The finding: **no worker on that board had ever loaded an MCP server**, across
> every attempt it has run.

## Why

A worker runs in a git worktree, and a worktree contains **tracked files only**. That is usually the right thing
— it is what makes a worktree a clean checkout. But a Claude Code project is configured in *two* files with
deliberately different lifetimes:

| file | tracked | reaches a worktree |
|---|---|---|
| `.mcp.json` | usually yes | **yes** |
| `.claude/settings.json` | yes | **yes** |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | **no**, gitignored | **never** |

MCP servers need both halves: `.mcp.json` *defines* them, and `enabledMcpjsonServers` /
`enableAllProjectMcpServers` *approves* them. Claude Code writes that approval into
`.claude/settings.local.json` — the per-developer file — because approving a server is a trust decision one
human made on one machine. Which is correct for a human, and silently wrong for a worker: the definitions
arrive, the approval does not, and **every MCP tool the board granted is inert**.

On pipao this had been true for the life of the board. `mcp__react-aria__*` sat in both profiles'
`allowed_tools`, so the board believed it had granted the server; `.mcp.json` defined `react-aria`, `supabase`
and `vercel`; and not one of the three ever appeared in a worker's tool calls. The failure it produced is the
one #130 was filed about — a worker building React components from training knowledge instead of the
component library sitting right there, and saying nothing — but the diagnosis in that card was **wrong**. It
was never denied. It was never there.

That is the general shape, and MCP is only its first instance: **a worker inherits the repo, and none of the
developer's approvals.** Anything Claude Code records in `settings.local.json` — approved servers, trusted
directories, remembered permission decisions — is invisible to every worker hkb launches, while the thing it
approves is right there in the worktree looking granted.

## What

- **`hkb doctor` names the split, not just the symptom.** The `mcp visibility` check (#130) reports that a
  server never appeared. It should also say *why* when it can: a server defined in `.mcp.json`, granted in a
  profile's `allowed_tools`, and approved **only** in `.claude/settings.local.json` is diagnosable from three
  files hkb can already read, and the fix is one line — move that entry into the tracked
  `.claude/settings.json`. Today the check says "check `.mcp.json` is readable", which is the wrong file.
- **`hkb init` should ask about it**, or at minimum report it: a repo with `.mcp.json` and approvals only in the
  local file is a board whose workers will silently have no MCP. Initialising is the moment a human is present
  and thinking about setup.
- **Audit the rest of `settings.local.json`** for anything else a worker needs and cannot inherit, and say so in
  one place. Approved MCP servers are what this card found; they are unlikely to be the only entry.
- **Do not have hkb write to `settings.local.json`.** It is the developer's file, hkb already refuses to put its
  hooks there (`init` moves them out on purpose), and the fix here is to tell a human which line to move, not to
  reach into a gitignored file on their behalf.
- Relationship to its neighbours, worth settling rather than assuming: #130 is the *detection* (a tool that was
  refused, or never showed up), #223 is the *posture* (how much power a worker may hold at all), and this is the
  *plumbing* between a repo's configuration and a worktree. All three touch `allowed_tools` and should not each
  grow their own answer.

## Done when

- [ ] `hkb doctor` distinguishes "the server was never approved for a worktree" from "the server was there and
      unused", and names the exact line to move and the file to move it to.
- [ ] A repo with `.mcp.json` whose approvals live only in `.claude/settings.local.json` is reported at `init`.
- [ ] The wiki page covering worker identity or the launch environment states the rule in one sentence: a worker
      inherits tracked files and no developer approvals.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass, with a test for the three-file diagnosis on a fixture repo.
goal: doctor tells an MCP server that was never approved for a worktree apart from one that was there and unused, naming the line to move and the tracked file to move it to; init reports the same at setup; the rule that a worker inherits tracked files and no developer approvals is written down
title: A worker inherits the repo but none of the developer's approvals, so an MCP server the board granted is never loaded and nothing says why
